config.title: Notification Context

intro.title: Notification Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification system for a React app using the Context API. You will learn how to create a context to manage and share notification state across different components without prop drilling. The core concepts include using React's Context API with TypeScript for type safety, managing state with useReducer, and displaying notifications with a custom component. You'll implement actions to add and remove notifications, ensuring a clean and reusable pattern for user feedback.
intro.usecase: A Notification Context is a foundational pattern for managing user-facing alerts across an entire React application, such as in e-commerce dashboards, admin panels, or financial platforms. It centralizes the display of success confirmations, error warnings, or system updates, eliminating repetitive alert logic in individual components like forms, data tables, or modals. This allows developers to trigger notifications from any component—like after a form submission or a data fetch—while maintaining a consistent, non-intrusive UI. Implementing this context is essential for building scalable, maintainable applications where user feedback needs to be coordinated and predictable.

objectives: Construct a NotificationContext using React's createContext API
Initialize and manage notification state with useState
Implement a NotificationProvider component to wrap the application
Configure a custom hook to access the notification context
Apply the notification context to components using the custom hook
Manipulate notification state to display and clear messages
Integrate the NotificationProvider into the main application component

steps.title: Define the Notification interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Notification' with three properties: 'id' (string), 'message' (string), and 'type' (a union type of 'info', 'success', 'warning', or 'error').
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. For the 'type' property, use a union type like 'type: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error''.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a Notification interface that defines the structure for notification objects used throughout the context.
successCriteria: The Notification interface is defined with id (string), message (string), and type ('info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error') properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your Notification interface includes all three properties: id (string), message (string), and type (with the four allowed string values).
steps.feedbackWrong: define a TypeScript interface named 'Notification' with the three specified properties and their types.

steps.hint: Use the createContext function you imported earlier. Provide the generic type and initial value as shown in the analogous example.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a typed context with null initial value
const ThemeContext = createContext<Theme | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a NotificationContext constant created with proper TypeScript typing and null initial value.
successCriteria: NotificationContext is created using createContext<NotificationContextType | null>(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
